title: TP Stall and Timeout Dashboard (Tensor Parallel Runtime) v1
author: Aisha Bello
body:
h1. Overview
The *TP Stall and Timeout* dashboard is how we detect and triage tensor-parallel (TP) stalls in the Serving Runtime. It is built to answer three questions fast:

1) *Is something stalling?* (heartbeat gaps / collectives not progressing)
2) *Where?* (replica, rank, model, cluster)
3) *Why, most likely?* (compute vs comms/NCCL vs scheduler starvation)

*SRE on-call* and *Serving Runtime on-call* use it during incidents and during canary rollouts (Dedicated first, then Hosted).

h2. Ownership and support model
* Dashboard owner (eng-platform/observability): *Aisha Bello*
* Dashboards and alert rules: *Sergio Costa*
* Runtime instrumentation: *Omar El-Sayed* (metrics/logs), *Julian Moore* (scheduler + load-shed integration)
* Paging policy / on-call readiness: *Rafael Mendes*

h3. Location
* Grafana folder: *Serving Runtime / TP Stability*
* Dashboard name: *TP Stalls & Request Timeouts (Multi-GPU)*
* Primary datasource: *Prometheus (metrics)*
* Secondary datasource: *Tracing (request spans)*
* Log correlation: *Structured runtime logs (replica_id, rank, request_id)*

h2. Required labels
Every metric backing a panel or alert must carry:

* *env:* prod | staging
* *deployment_mode:* hosted | dedicated | private
* *cluster:* (e.g., us-east1-a, eu-west1-b)
* *service:* serving-runtime
* *model:* catalog id (e.g., llama-70b, mixtral-8x7b)
* *tp_degree:* 2 | 4 | 8
* *replica_id:* runtime replica identifier
* *rank:* TP rank index (0..tp_degree-1)

If a section shows “No data”, look at the *Missing instrumentation* panel and confirm the runtime build emits TP heartbeats and stall reason codes.

h1. Metric glossary
Naming follows the convention agreed between eng-runtime and SRE. Components still using earlier names are mapped by the compatibility recording rules in the dashboard folder.

* *redwood_tp_rank_heartbeat_ts_seconds{...}* — last heartbeat timestamp per TP rank.
* *redwood_tp_stall_reason_total{reason=..., ...}* — detected stall reasons (runtime taxonomy).
* *redwood_tp_inflight_collectives{collective=..., ...}* — in-flight collectives gauge.
* *redwood_tp_collective_progress_steps_total{collective=..., ...}* — progress counter for no-progress detection.
* *redwood_runtime_request_timeouts_total{route=..., streaming=..., ...}* — request timeouts.
* *redwood_runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket{...}* — request latency histogram.
* *redwood_nccl_errors_total{code=..., ...}* — NCCL errors surfaced to the runtime.
* *redwood_runtime_replica_drains_total{reason=..., ...}* — drain events, watchdog included.
* *redwood_tp_watchdog_aborts_total{stage=prefill|decode|collective, ...}* — watchdog aborts.
* *redwood_scheduler_queue_depth{queue=..., ...}* — scheduler queue depth (prefill/decode/collective).
* *redwood_overload_rejects_total{reason=tp_stall|capacity|...}* — load-shedding / overload rejects.

h1. Dashboard structure and panels
h2. 1) Executive summary (top row)
Use these to confirm an incident is real.

* *TP stall indicator (composite):* % of replicas with a rank heartbeat gap over threshold OR collective no-progress.
* *Request timeouts rate:* timeouts/min overall and per deployment_mode.
* *p95/p99 request latency:* streaming vs non-streaming.
* *Replica drains (last 1h):* drains/min stacked by reason.

h3. Reference PromQL
* Heartbeat gap (seconds):
  * max by (replica_id, tp_degree, model, cluster) (time() - redwood_tp_rank_heartbeat_ts_seconds)
* Timeout rate:
  * sum by (deployment_mode, model) (rate(redwood_runtime_request_timeouts_total[5m]))

h2. 2) TP heartbeat and rank health
Find the wedged replica/rank.

* *Heartbeat gap heatmap (by replica_id)*
* *Worst ranks table:* top N (replica_id, rank) by heartbeat gap
* *Heartbeat gap distribution:* per-replica max gap histogram
* *Missing heartbeat series:* ranks that stopped reporting (exporter death vs real stall)

h3. Notes
* A heartbeat gap alone does not prove a stall; confirm with timeouts and collective progress.
* One rank missing while the others progress usually means *rank divergence* (often KV/cache edge cases).

h2. 3) Collective progress and NCCL / comms signals
* *In-flight collectives* by type (allreduce, allgather, reducescatter).
* *Collective no-progress detector:* replicas whose progress counter is flat for > X seconds.
* *NCCL error rate:* errors/min by code and cluster.
* *NCCL debug enabled annotation:* windows with extra NCCL debug logging.

h3. Interpretation guide
* Heartbeat gap + stuck in-flight collective + rising NCCL errors => *comms boundary / ordering mismatch*.
* Heartbeat gap + no NCCL errors + growing scheduler queue => *scheduler starvation / fairness*.
* Timeouts spiking without heartbeat gaps => *routing, overload, or client cancellations*.

h2. 4) Scheduler and backpressure
* *Scheduler queue depth (prefill/decode/collective)*, stacked.
* *Scheduler starvation flags* from stall_reason.
* *Batch composition* (prefill-heavy vs mixed vs decode-heavy), where emitted.

h2. 5) Request impact correlation
* *Timeouts by route and streaming*.
* *Timeout correlation table:* replicas with high heartbeat gap vs timeouts in the same cluster/model.
* *Client cancellations (if available)* for cancellation-path deadlocks.

h2. 6) Mitigation and “blast radius” controls
* *Watchdog aborts* by stage and model.
* *Replica drains* by reason, drain storms highlighted.
* *Load-shedding / overload rejects* with reason=tp_stall.
* *Fallback routing events*, if enabled.

h1. Alert rules (definitions, thresholds, routing)
Alerts fall into (A) paging, (B) ticket-only, (C) informational. Values are *prod* defaults; clusters/models can override via alert rule labels.

h2. A) Paging alerts (Sev2, may escalate to Sev1)
1) *TPHeartbeatGapCritical*
* Condition: max heartbeat gap per replica > *45s* for *5m* AND request timeouts rate elevated.
* Route: *SRE On-call (page)* + *Serving Runtime On-call (page)*
* Runbook: confluence://eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-tp-hang-mitigation

2) *TPCollectiveNoProgress*
* Condition: collective progress counter flat for > *20s* on any replica for *2m*.
* Route: *SRE On-call (page)* + *Kernel on-call* (via runtime on-call)
* Notes: Sensitive by design; tune per tp_degree if it gets noisy.

3) *TPRequestTimeoutSpike*
* Condition: timeouts/min > baseline × *4* for *10m* (per cluster+model), OR absolute timeouts/min > *50* for *10m*.
* Route: *SRE On-call (page)*

h2. B) Ticket-only alerts
4) *NCCLErrorRateHigh*
* Condition: NCCL errors/min > *1* for *15m* (per cluster).
* Route: *Runtime kernels triage queue* (Linear) + notify #eng-runtime.

5) *ReplicaDrainStormTP*
* Condition: drains/min > *5* for *20m* with reason matching tp_watchdog|tp_stall.
* Route: *SRE ticket* + notify #eng-sre.

6) *LoadShedDueToTPStallHigh*
* Condition: overload rejects with reason=tp_stall > *10/min* for *15m*.
* Route: *SRE ticket* + notify #eng-runtime.

h2. C) Informational alerts
7) *MissingTPHeartbeatMetrics*
* Condition: expected rank heartbeats absent for > *5m* after the replica is Ready.
* Route: *Observability team Slack*, ticket if it persists.

h1. Alert routing and escalation policy
h2. Paging targets
* Primary: *SRE On-call* (PagerDuty: “Runtime Platform - Prod”)
* Secondary: *Serving Runtime On-call* (PagerDuty: “Runtime Core”)
* FYI channels: #eng-runtime, #eng-sre

h2. Escalation triggers
Open an incident channel and consider Sev1 if:
* TPHeartbeatGapCritical fires for > 15 minutes in a Dedicated enterprise cluster.
* Timeouts exceed 2% of requests for > 10 minutes in prod.
* Several clusters show correlated collective no-progress.

h1. Operational notes
h2. Annotations and deploy markers
Shown on the dashboard: runtime version rollouts (canary start/end), feature-flag changes (e.g., tp_watchdog_enabled), and NCCL debug logging windows. During canaries, check whether changes line up with a heavier heartbeat gap tail, drain storms, or more load-shedding.

h2. Common false positives
* *Exporter/agent restart:* heartbeat series reset; check pod restarts and MissingTPHeartbeatMetrics.
* *Low traffic:* progress metrics can look flat; compare with request rate.
* *Intentional drain:* maintenance can cause drain spikes without stalls.

h2. Data retention and resolution
* Metrics resolution: 10s
* Retention: 7 days (standard), 30 days for selected recorded series (TP stall indicators)

h1. Quick triage checklist (on-call)
1) Confirm customer impact using the timeout rate and p99 latency panels.
2) Find the worst replica(s) with the heartbeat heatmap and worst ranks table.
3) Narrow the cause: collective no-progress => comms/NCCL (check NCCL errors and deploy markers); rising queue depth without NCCL signals => scheduler starvation/backpressure.
4) Mitigate per runbook: drain affected replicas, temporarily lower concurrency caps / batch sizes, or flag off a newly rolled-out TP kernel path.
5) Before recycling, capture: screenshots of the last 5–10 minutes of panels, replica_id, rank, model, tp_degree, runtime version and active TP flags.

h1. Change log
* 2025-01-28: First published version (A. Bello) with heartbeat and timeout correlation panels.
* 2025-02-12: Added collective no-progress detector and drain storm alert (S. Costa).
